solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plot prepared by criminals, leading to robbery at sea

parts.note: cons are convicts, short for convicted criminals
piracy is robbery committed on the high seas

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks hatches a scheme ending in a raid on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret scheme by a group, which is exactly what a plot is.

clue.text: Audience's drink finds clown!

indicators.note: what an audience gets is what it hears, so the drink is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: cocoa is a hot chocolate drink, and its final A is silent

explanation.surface: Someone in the stands orders a drink and spots a clown at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco was a famous circus clown, Nicolai Poliakoff, who performed in Britain for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco the Clown was a celebrated Russian-born circus performer, so the name stands as an example of a clown.

clue.text: It may be Blue or White, nothing else to begin with

definitions.text: It may be Blue or White

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter only of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of else

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something that can be blue or white with nothing else to start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Nile and the White Nile are the two great branches of the river, meeting at Khartoum.

clue.text: Stingy priest clutching the writer's promissory notes

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so the priest wraps round what follows

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest
the writer is the setter, I, and 'the writer's' is read as I'M, I am
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A mean clergyman keeps a firm grip on the IOUs the narrator signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' in a crossword is the setter, so 'the writer's' becomes 'I am' shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimonious describes someone extremely unwilling to spend money, a close synonym for stingy.

clue.text: Charge pounds to see a musteline mammal

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone pays an entrance fee in pounds to view an animal at a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Musteline means of the weasel family; the ratel is the honey badger.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, belongs to the weasel family Mustelidae, hence musteline.

clue.text: Working doctor with niece regularly wearing tiara

indicators.note: working suggests something being worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of niece

explanation.surface: A doctor on duty is accompanied by his niece, who is wearing a tiara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working doctor' reads as a practising physician, but 'Working' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown or tiara, so coroneted means adorned with one.

clue.text: One who wrote of love endlessly, in detail at first

indicators.note: without ends means the word loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: love with its outer letters removed

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of in and detail

explanation.surface: A tribute to a poet who wrote about love at length and in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who wrote of love' looks like the whole definition, and it fits the poet of the Ars Amatoria, but love is also the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses and the Art of Love, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Poems about a sick French king's palace

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the poems go around the words that follow

parts.note: verses are poems
taken as written
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A collection of verses about an ailing king of France and his royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French king' looks like part of the wordplay, perhaps ROI, but the definition is the whole of 'French king's palace'.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles was the grand palace built by Louis XIV, the French king's seat outside Paris.

clue.text: Followed loch, showing persistence

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Someone trailed around a Scottish lake, perhaps hunting for its monster, with great perseverance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggedness is tenacious determination, the quality of keeping going, which is persistence.

clue.text: State having abandoned function backed a routine singing style

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so those letters are taken out of the state

parts.note: Colorado is a US state
a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the following words are read in reverse

parts.note: A plus RUT, a rut being a dull routine

explanation.surface: A state official ditches a party and runs through a routine backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: COLORADO drops its DO to leave COLORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloratura is elaborate ornamented vocal music with runs and trills, a style of operatic singing.

clue.text: Republican overwhelmed by giant drink

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it ends up inside the following word

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is beaten by a towering opponent, then reaches for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giants of British legend, their effigies kept at London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog is rum diluted with water, once the sailor's ration, so a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: How obscure coteries all stray, ultimately?

definitions.text: How obscure coteries all stray, ultimately?

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so these letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of stray

explanation.surface: A question about the obscure manner in which exclusive cliques eventually drift apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Stray works twice: as the anagram signal and, through ultimately, as the source of the last letter. The whole clue then describes how secretive coteries behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterically means in a way understood only by a small inner circle, which is how a clique keeps things obscure.

clue.text: Old fish market scandal over presentation of accounts?

parts.note: billing is sending out bills, a playful reading of presenting accounts
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, from Watergate

explanation.surface: A historic market caught up in a row over how its books were presented.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLINGS then GATE; the question mark flags the whimsical sense of accounts. Billingsgate was London's main fish market, moved from the City in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate was the famous London fish market by the Thames, now relocated, so the old site is an old fish market.

clue.text: Garden designer touches down with something that may be cut

parts.note: an aircraft that touches down lands
to cut a caper is to leap or dance playfully

explanation.surface: A gardener arrives by air bringing a plant that can be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something that may be cut' suggests a hedge or lawn, but it is the caper in the idiom cut a caper.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscaper plans and lays out gardens and grounds, so is a garden designer.

clue.text: One sits out with everyone on river

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
all means everyone
crossword sense: a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: Someone sits out by the river with all their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first pieces above the last. A flower here is a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is a shy person who sits out the dancing at a party, watching from the side.

clue.text: Expert in body of stories — first about cat

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person
a tom is a male cat
1st, read as IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone well versed in a body of stories, the first of them about a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of stories' looks like one unit, but body belongs to the definition. 'About' simply places the first beside the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist studies the structure of the human body, so is an expert on it.

clue.text: Curious airs displayed by chosen member of ancient ethnic group

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so these letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters of airs rearranged
the elite are the chosen few

explanation.surface: A member of a chosen people shows strange airs.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew people descended from Jacob, called Israel.

clue.text: Weapon used by bird of prey in brutal onslaught

definitions.text: Weapon used by bird of prey

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of brutal into onslaught

explanation.surface: A hawk swoops on its prey, its weapon used in a savage attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a raptor, the weapon with which it seizes prey.

clue.text: Capital husband invested in food retail outlet

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so this letter goes within the outlet

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells prepared food
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband puts his money into a delicatessen business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'invested' make a finance picture, but Capital is the definition: a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, or New Delhi within it, is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Haggard chap with singular description of horse without jockey

definitions.text: Haggard chap with singular description of horse without jockey

parts.note: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines, and Rider is his name
-less means without, as in hopeless

explanation.surface: A worn-out man gives an odd account of a horse that has lost its jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggard looks like an adjective for a weary chap; it is the novelist. The whole clue also hints at the answer: the chap's name plus 'without' makes a peculiar word for a horse with no jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse running on after unseating its jockey is said to be riderless, having nobody on its back.

clue.text: Unsettling experience involving lab specimens and wine

parts.note: cultures are microorganisms grown for study in a lab
hock is British for German white wine, from Hochheim

explanation.surface: A disturbing incident in a laboratory involving samples and some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture shock is the disorientation felt on meeting an unfamiliar way of life, an unsettling experience.

clue.text: Trick old copper in outskirts of Hastings

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the edges that follow
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the town are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Hastings
O is the abbreviation for old
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A veteran policeman plays a trick on the edge of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old copper' sounds like a retired policeman, but it is two pieces, O and the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To hocus someone is to trick or hoax them, as in hocus-pocus.

clue.text: Church body a Welshman set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means lifted from bottom to top, so the name reads upwards

parts.note: Evan is a common Welsh man's name, so a Welshman

explanation.surface: A Welshman founds a church organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church body' looks like a congregation or synod, but it is the main body of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the central part of a church where the congregation sits, its main body.

clue.text: Extremely happy and profitable promotion

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, so only the outermost letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of happy
the first and last letters of profitable

explanation.surface: A marketing campaign that leaves everyone very happy and makes plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant publicity, a form of promotion for a product or event.

clue.text: Man on board's obscene material spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so the word sounds like it but is spelt otherwise

parts.note: porn is obscene material; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: A crew member on a ship is caught with dirty magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor, but the board is a chessboard and pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is the lowliest chess piece, and chess pieces are called men, so a man on the board.

clue.text: Various items: a lot seen around one's place of confinement

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps around the rest

parts.note: many means a lot
one is I, so one's is I'S
a cell is a room where a prisoner is confined

explanation.surface: An inmate's cell holds a mixed collection of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as I plus the apostrophe-S, giving two letters rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of assorted things, so various items gathered together.

clue.text: Splendid introduction to radio — live

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of radio
to live is to be, and are is a form of be

explanation.surface: An excellent start to a live radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like broadcast live, rhyming with five; read it as the verb to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare in an old-fashioned sense means excellent or fine, as in a rare old time.

clue.text: Fine woollen cloth Irish found in Kentucky pool

indicators.note: found in places the language inside the state abbreviation that follows

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland
a mere is a small lake or pool

explanation.surface: A fine Irish fabric turns up in a swimming pool in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerseymere is a fine twilled woollen fabric, a lighter variant of kersey cloth.
